        local path or a remote fsspec URL (``gs://bucket/survey/raw``); a
        remote folder is listed without downloading any data.
    calibration_outputs_string: Subdirectory name for calibration artifacts. When
        running inside the recipe executor this is resolved relative to the pipeline's
        user-facing outputs directory (``artifacts_dir`` from the execution context)
        so calibration files land alongside images and logs under ``outputs/``.
        Falls back to a CWD-relative path when called standalone (e.g. in a notebook).
        Calibration JSON logs are written to a ``logs/`` subdirectory within this
        folder (i.e. ``<calibration_outputs>/logs/``).
    raw_file_names: Optional list of specific raw file name strings to process.
        If empty or None, all .raw files in raw_input_folder are used.
    clear_previous_json_logs: If True, delete existing calibration_flags.json (default: True).
    file_time_start: Optional inclusive lower bound (ISO string or datetime)
        on each raw file's recording span. The span is inferred from the
        ``D{YYYYMMDD}-T{HHMMSS}`` name stamps: a file's own stamp is its
        start and the next file's stamp is its end, so a file that starts
        before this bound but records into the window is kept. Filtering is
        name-based except for the single file straddling this bound, whose
        real end is read from its datagram headers so a gap between survey
        legs is not mistaken for one long recording.
    file_time_end: Optional inclusive upper bound; see *file_time_start*.

Returns:
    dict with keys:
        raw_file_paths: list[str] of absolute paths (or gs:// URLs) to raw

source.doc:
Concatenate a list of xarray Datasets along a dimension.

Reconsolidation (fan-in) helper for the recipe system's ``collect``
pattern: a mapped step that produces one Dataset per data segment (e.g.
per-file MVBS) is gathered into a list, and this joins them back into one
Dataset along ``dim`` (default ``ping_time``).

A single Dataset (not a list) is returned unchanged so a ``map_over``
source that resolves to one item still works (single-item transparency).

Only variables that already have ``dim`` are concatenated. Variables
without it (e.g. an Sv dataset's ``frequency_nominal`` on ``(channel,)``,
or a scalar ``sound_speed``) are taken from the first segment and keep
their original shape. ``xarray.concat``'s default (``data_vars="all"``)
would instead broadcast every variable along ``dim``, turning
``frequency_nominal`` into ``(ping_time, channel)`` and scalars into
``(ping_time,)`` -- which silently corrupts the schema for downstream
consumers that expect per-channel metadata to stay 1-D.

Note that per-segment metadata differences are therefore resolved in
favour of the first segment: if segments were calibrated with different
environmental parameters, the merged dataset records the first segment's
``sound_speed``/``sound_absorption``. The data variables themselves are
unaffected -- each segment's values were already computed with its own
parameters.

The provenance variables in :data:`_PROVENANCE_CONCAT_VARS` are exempt
from that rule: taking only the first segment's ``source_filenames``
would make a survey merged from many raw files claim a single source, so
they are concatenated along their own dimension to list every
contributing file.

Args:
    datasets: A list of ``xarray.Dataset`` objects, or a single Dataset.
    dim: Dimension to concatenate along. Defaults to ``"ping_time"``.
    on_duplicate: What to do when segments share a label on *dim*.
        ``None`` (default) leaves them, which is right when the segments
        cannot overlap. ``"mean"`` averages them into one entry, which is
        what a fan-in over per-segment *binned* products needs: see
        :func:`_combine_duplicate_labels`. ``"first"`` keeps the first and
        sorts, which is what a fan-in over overlapping *slices of one
        store* needs: see :func:`_drop_duplicate_labels`.
    **kwargs: Forwarded to :func:`xarray.concat`, and override the
        defaults set here.

Returns:
    A single concatenated ``xarray.Dataset``.

Raises:
    ValueError: If ``datasets`` is an empty collection.

ops.description:
Detect the seafloor with a phase-aware dynamic-programming line picker and return a 1-D (ping_time,) DataArray of the seabed echo's leading edge in metres. On the primary channel the detector finds phase-stable, loud seed regions, scores every sample inside a search window on Sv, local phase stability, echo asymmetry, SNR and the leading-edge energy gradient (Mode 1 of the v4 design; ``mode: 2`` adds the below-versus-above Sv contrast, below-region stationarity and below-region phase activity, for when dense near-bottom aggregations are confused with the seabed), then runs a Viterbi pass over the top score maxima per ping with a Huber transition whose break-point scales with the distance the vessel travelled between pings. The pick is walked back to the -10 dB point of the echo. A forward-backward pass gives a confidence and margin per ping.
Drop-in swap with the ``detect_seafloor``, ``ep_detect_seafloor``, ``read_seafloor_line`` and ``hdbscan_detect_seafloor`` ops: the output port name (``seafloor_depth``) and shape (1-D, ping_time) match, so ``create_seafloor_mask`` works unchanged. By default the line is the leading edge, not an integration line; put the dead-zone offset in ``create_seafloor_mask``'s ``seafloor_buffer_m``. ``line: integration`` returns the Ona-Mitson backstepped line with the slope correction instead, which on the HB1603 canyon walls clears the up-slope echo that a 10 m buffer above the leading edge left in the 18 kHz channel. Every intermediate is available through ``diagnostics_path``.
The op is self-contained: with no window or prior given it first runs a fast slab estimator (Mode 0b) over the whole recorded range, which averages a few dozen slabs of pings, scores them and joins them with the same line search, adding slabs where the seabed moves; its line and uncertainty become the per-ping search window for the full detector. ``r_min`` / ``r_max`` bound that search and ``z_prior`` replaces it.
Split-beam angles come from ``ds_Sv`` when ``ep_add_splitbeam_angle`` ran upstream. Without them the detector runs amplitude-only with a warning: seeds are picked on Sv and extent alone, so a dense aggregation can be taken for the seabed. Pings where no candidate clears ``min_score`` are bridged by the line search and interpolated up to ``max_gap_s``; longer runs and the ends of the file stay NaN, which ``create_seafloor_mask`` masks entirely. Aliased-seabed detection is off by default: it is single-channel only and on HB1603 the water-column angle noise alone tripped it and the mask covered the true seabed.
Measured 2026-09-24 on one file each: HB1603 38 kHz at 1750 m (EK60, 8 s pinging) followed the seabed through a 100 m step with a median 8 m offset above the .bot line, which itself sits below the Sv rise; HB2407 18 kHz at 57 m (EK80) sat 2 m below the Echoview line with no gross errors. inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Calibrated Sv dataset with ``echo_range`` and the ``tau_effective``, ``sound_speed`` and beamwidth variables that ``compute_sv`` attaches. inputs.name: echodata
inputs.description: Accepted for interface parity with the other seafloor detection ops; not read.

inputs.name: z_prior
inputs.description: Optional expected seabed depth per ping, for example another detector's ``seafloor_depth`` or a survey line, on any ping grid. It sets the per-ping search window to z_prior +/- 3 sigma_prior_m and overrides r_min / r_max where they conflict.

outputs.description: Seabed leading edge in metres, shape (ping_time,), on ds_Sv's exact ping_time coordinate. Attributes record the vertical reference, the primary channel, the regime preset, ping coverage and the number of flagged and interpolated pings.

params.name: channel
params.description: Primary channel as its label, or its frequency in Hz or kHz given as a string (e.g. "38"). Null picks the lowest frequency channel whose seeds span at least a fifth of the pings, falling back to the lowest frequency with a warning.

params.name: r_min
params.description: Lower bound of the search window on the dataset's range reference. Default 10 m past the first sample, which skips the transmit pulse.

params.name: r_max
params.description: Upper bound of the search window. Default the end of the channel's range. Set both bounds on deep surveys: the crop they define is what keeps a 15000-sample ping affordable.

params.name: sigma_prior_m
params.description: Uncertainty of z_prior; default 2 % of z_prior. Ignored without it.

params.name: regime
params.description: Depth regime preset: "shelf" (< 200 m), "slope" (200 to 1000 m), "deep" (> 1000 m) or "auto" from the search window midpoint. Sets the SNR reference, the seed Sv floor and the Mode 2 shape window.

params.name: mode
params.description: Scoring mode. 1 scores the six point features; 2 adds the three local shape features (Stage 3b), which cost a little more and help where a school sits on the bottom. Both are deterministic.

params.name: line
params.description: "leading_edge" (default) or "integration": which line to return on the seafloor_depth port. See the description.

params.name: prior
params.description: "auto" (default) runs the Mode 0 slab estimator when no z_prior is given and uses it as the search window; "none" searches only the fixed r_min / r_max window.

params.name: missing
params.description: What a ping with no seabed found gets after gap filling. "nan" (default) leaves it NaN and create_seafloor_mask masks the ping entirely, which an analysis wants. "max_range" sets it to the last recorded range so the ping is kept whole, which a survey picture wants where the seabed is sometimes below the recording. ping_coverage still counts detections.

params.name: min_seabed_sv_db
params.description: A pick whose mean Sv over the pulse length below it is under this is rejected as not seabed, both in the prior's slabs and in the final line. The scores are relative to each ping, so without a floor a file whose seabed lies beyond the recorded range picks its loudest scattering layer instead (on HB1603, a -57 dB layer just past the near field). Seabed echoes on HB1603 and HB2407 run -13 to -40 dB. Null disables the check.

params.name: prior_budget
params.description: Slab budget for the Mode 0 estimator. Each slab reads a few pings across the range; on a zarr store chunked along ping_time a slab costs one chunk read.

params.name: n_candidates
params.description: Score maxima kept per ping for the line search.

params.name: max_slope_deg
params.description: Maximum plausible seabed slope. With the distance travelled between pings it sets the depth change the transition cost treats as ordinary; larger jumps are tolerated at linear cost. Use 45 on rocky or canyon terrain.

params.name: alpha
params.description: Transition strength multiplier in [0.5, 2].

params.name: beta_fraction
params.description: Shallow-first tie-break prior as a fraction of the candidate score spread; 0 disables it. Targets ghost bottoms and the echo tail.

params.name: min_score
params.description: Candidates below this score are dropped; a ping with none is skipped and bridged. Scores are sums of tanh terms, so 0 means neutral.

params.name: walkback_db
params.description: Drop below the echo peak that marks the leading edge.

params.name: effective_beamwidth_deg
params.description: Effective beamwidth for the backstepped integration line in the diagnostics; default nominal times 12/7 (the ES38B ratio).

params.name: vessel_speed_m_s
params.description: Speed used for along-track distance when ds_Sv carries no latitude and longitude. Without either, the break-point falls to one pulse length per ping, which suits a station but over-smooths a transect.

params.name: min_confidence
params.description: Pings whose posterior confidence is below this are flagged.

params.name: phase_weight
params.description: Weight of the two phase features. Raise to 1.5 where fish aggregations are the main confuser.

params.name: max_gap_s
params.description: Interior runs of skipped pings up to this long are interpolated; longer runs stay NaN. Null interpolates nothing.

params.name: transition
params.description: "huber" or "truncated" (quadratic capped at the break-point, for cliffs).

params.name: pulse_length_s
params.description: Pulse duration when ds_Sv has no tau_effective.

params.name: beamwidth_deg
params.description: Nominal beamwidth when ds_Sv has none.

params.name: detect_aliases
params.description: Run the single-channel Blackwell aliased-seabed detector and exclude its mask. See the description before enabling it.

params.name: phase_threshold_deg2
params.description: Seed phase-stability threshold on the summed angle variance within one pulse length; default (beamwidth / 2)^2.

params.name: confidence_tolerance_pulses
params.description: Alternatives within this many pulse lengths of the pick (plus the beam-geometry spread, or inside the same loud run) count as the same pick when computing confidence and margin.

params.name: diagnostics_path
params.description: Optional zarr path for the full diagnostics: masks, features, score, candidates, raw pick, leading edge, backstepped integration line, confidence, margin and flags on the cropped grid. Local runs only; the path is written as given.

ops.description:
Choose ping ranges that a pyramid can be built over independently and then concatenated exactly.
A pyramid is a reduction along the ping axis, so it splits along that axis, but only if the cuts fall on the reduction's own cell boundaries. Level k merges 2**k pings, so every range but the last is a multiple of 2**(levels-1) and reduces to a whole number of cells at every level. The last range is whatever is left: its final cell is short, which is exactly what a serial build produces at the end of a survey, so the segmented result is not an approximation of the serial one but the same answer.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Sv Dataset, read only for its ping count.

outputs.name: ranges
outputs.description: List of [start, stop] ping ranges, in order and tiling the survey with no gap or overlap. Map build_echogram_pyramid over this.

outputs.name: grid
outputs.description: The multiple the ranges are aligned to, which is 2**(levels-1).

params.name: levels
params.description: Levels the build will produce, which is what sets the grid.

params.name: target_pings
params.description: Rough segment size, rounded down onto the grid. Sized for the memory one mapped instance needs: a segment is held whole while its levels are reduced, so at five channels and an uncropped water column 32,768 pings is roughly a gigabyte at level zero and twice that through the cascade. Raise it for a wide machine, lower it for a deep water column.

ops.description: Render a full clustering report for one or more clustering results. Produces the clustering echogram, per-cluster statistics report, and the HDBSCAN hierarchy plot when the clustering result includes a model and hierarchy plotting is applicable. This is a sink step: it produces figures with no data output.

inputs.name: ds_normalized
inputs.description: Embedded normalized ML Dataset containing stored cluster-label variables

inputs.name: clustering_results
inputs.description: Clustering result Dataset from run_hdbscan or assign_clusters_to_all_points. Legacy dict results and collected lists are also accepted (many: true). Optional: every panel but the HDBSCAN hierarchy reads the labels embed_clustering_results stored in ds_normalized, so a report can be drawn from that checkpointed dataset alone and the fit never has to be rerun for it. params.description: Sv variable name used when computing per-cluster statistics, or "ml_features" to plot the flattened ML features used for clustering

params.description: Compute inter-channel diffs in cluster statistics, taken against the second-lowest-frequency channel

Render the full clustering report for one or more clustering results.

Set ``cluster_stats_sv_data_var='ml_features'`` to plot statistics for
the flattened ML features used by clustering instead of gridded Sv channel
values.

The cluster statistics figure carries a lot of small text, so it is
rendered at ``cluster_stats_dpi`` rather than the report-wide ``dpi``
used by the much larger echogram. Pass None to tie it back to ``dpi``.

``time_min`` and ``time_max`` window the echogram by UTC timestamp,
taking precedence over the ping bounds in ``plot_window``. Pair them with
``x_axis_units='datetime'`` to label the axis with clock times.

``overlay_windows`` draws line files onto the echogram per window: each
window's files under ``overlay_window_keys`` (the three dive-profile keys
by default) are read onto that window's own pings, so every window is a
separate segment and overlapping windows each keep their own line.

``overlay_fit_style`` and ``overlay_bound_style`` are matplotlib keyword
dicts for the fitted profile and for its two confidence bounds. Each is
merged over the built-in style, so naming only ``color`` restyles the

Plot ML-processed echogram data (regular Sv-derived or MVBS-derived).

Automatically detects MVBS format and handles both regular Sv and MVBS-based ML data.
For MVBS-derived ML data, ``ds_Sv_original`` is required for proper ping range
conversion.

Args:
    ds_ml (xarray.Dataset): Dataset containing ML data (must have flattened
        ML features).
    ml_dataset_name (str): Name of the ML dataset variable
        (e.g., ``'ml_data_clean'``).
    ds_Sv_original (xarray.Dataset, optional): Original Sv dataset (required
        for MVBS-derived ML data to convert ping indices).
    frequency_nominal (array-like, optional): Nominal frequencies.
        Auto-detected from ML features if ``None``.
    ml_specific_data_name (str, optional): Specific ML data name within
        dataset (e.g., ``'normalized'``).
    min_depth (float, optional): Minimum depth in meters.
        Auto-detected from data if ``None``.
    max_depth (float, optional): Maximum depth in meters.
        Auto-detected from data if ``None``.
    ping_min (int, optional): Start ping index. Defaults to 0.
        For MVBS-derived: in ORIGINAL Sv indices (converted to MVBS bins).
    ping_max (int, optional): End ping index. Defaults to last ping.
    time_min (str or datetime, optional): Start of the displayed window as
        a UTC timestamp, resolved to the closest ping. Takes precedence
        over ``ping_min``.
    time_max (str or datetime, optional): End of the displayed window as a
        UTC timestamp, resolved to the closest ping. Takes precedence over
        ``ping_max``.
    ml_vmin (float, optional): Minimum color scale limit.
        Auto-detected from data if ``None``.
    ml_vmax (float, optional): Maximum color scale limit.
        Auto-detected from data if ``None``.
    sv_cmap (str): Colormap name. Defaults to ``'viridis'``.
    x_axis_units (str): X-axis units: ``'datetime'`` (default, absolute UTC
        clock times), ``'seconds'`` from the first ping shown, ``'pings'``,
        ``'bins'`` (MVBS only), or ``'meters'``.
    y_axis_units (str): Y-axis units: ``'meters'``, ``'range_sample'``, or
        ``'bins'`` (MVBS only).
    meters_per_second (float, optional): Speed for ``'meters'`` x-axis
        (auto-calculated from GPS if ``echodata`` provided).
    echodata (xarray.Dataset, optional): Original echodata for GPS-based
        calculations.
    y_to_x_aspect_ratio_override (float, optional): Force each panel to be
        this many times wider than tall, bypassing the automatic clamp.
    overlay_lines (list, optional): List of line specification dicts for
        overlay lines.

    >>> # Basic usage - regular Sv-derived ML
    >>> plot_flattened_data_echogram(ds_ml, 'ml_data_clean')
    
    >>> # Basic usage - MVBS-derived ML
    >>> plot_flattened_data_echogram(ds_ml_mvbs, 'ml_data_clean',
    ...                             ds_Sv_original=ds_Sv)
    
    >>> # With specific ML data and custom color range
    >>> plot_flattened_data_echogram(ds_ml, 'ml_data_clean',
    ...                             ml_specific_data_name='normalized',
    ...                             ml_vmin=-2, ml_vmax=2)
    
    >>> # MVBS-derived with custom ping range (in original Sv indices)
    >>> plot_flattened_data_echogram(ds_ml_mvbs, 'ml_data_clean',
    ...                             ds_Sv_original=ds_Sv,
    ...                             ping_min=100, ping_max=800)

    >>> plot_flattened_data_echogram(ds_ml_mvbs, 'ml_data_clean',
    ...                             ds_Sv_original=ds_Sv,
    ...                             x_axis_units='bins', y_axis_units='bins')
    
    >>> # With custom depth range
    >>> plot_flattened_data_echogram(ds_ml, 'features',
    ...                             min_depth=10, max_depth=100)

source.doc:
Query the NOAA NCEI Water Column Sonar Data (WCSD) archive.

Searches the WCSD ArcGIS MapServer for sonar data files matching the given
criteria.  All parameters are optional; omit a parameter to leave that
field unconstrained.

Args:
    dataset_name (str | None): Dataset identifier, e.g. ``'DY2207_EK80'``.
    instrument_type (str | None): Instrument name substring, e.g. ``'EK80'``.
    frequencies (list[str] | None): Frequency strings to match,
        e.g. ``['18WKHZ', '38WKHZ']``.  Results must contain *any* of the
        listed frequencies (OR logic).
    calibration_state (int | list[int] | None): Calibration state value(s),
        e.g. ``4`` for "Calibrated w/ calibration data".
    collection_start (str | None): Inclusive start date as ``'YYYY-MM-DD'``.
        Filters the server-side ``COLLECTION_DATE`` field (day-level
        granularity).
    collection_end (str | None): Inclusive end date as ``'YYYY-MM-DD'``.
    file_time_start (str | datetime | None): Inclusive start datetime for
        fine-grained filtering.  Each file's recording span is inferred
        from the filename timestamps (``D{YYYYMMDD}-T{HHMMSS}``): its own
        stamp is the recording start and the next file's stamp (within
        the same dataset) is its end.  Files whose span overlaps the
        window are kept, so a file that starts before this bound but
        records into the window is included.  A dataset's last file has
        no inferred end and is kept only when its own stamp is inside the
        window.  Accepts an ISO-format string or a ``datetime`` object.
    file_time_end (str | datetime | None): Inclusive end datetime for
        fine-grained filtering (same format as *file_time_start*).
    max_files (int | None): Maximum number of results to return.  Applied
        after all other filters; results are sorted chronologically by
        filename timestamp.
    bbox (tuple | None): Bounding box ``(west, south, east, north)`` in
        WGS 84 decimal degrees. Applied server-side as an ArcGIS
        envelope-intersection filter against each file's own track
        polyline, so every file whose track passes through the box is
        returned (including tracks that cross a corner between vertices).
    center_point (tuple | None): ``(longitude, latitude)`` for a
        radius-based spatial query.
    radius_nm (float | None): Search radius in nautical miles (requires
        *center_point*).
    filters (dict | None): Additional field-level filters as
        ``{FIELD_NAME: value}`` pairs.  Each becomes an exact-match clause
        in the query.  Use this for any WCSD attribute not covered by the
        explicit parameters above (e.g.
        ``{'CRUISE_NAME': 'DY2207', 'PLATFORM_NAME': 'Oscar Dyson (DY)'}``).
    return_geometry (bool): Whether each record should include its track
        ``GEOMETRY``. Defaults to ``True`` (the geometry adds negligible
        query time). Set ``False`` to omit it and keep the returned
        records / checkpoints smaller. Geometry is always returned for
        spatial queries (``bbox`` or ``center_point``) regardless of this
        flag.
    file_names (list[str] | None): Keep only these files, matched on the
        ``D{date}-T{time}`` stamp in the name, so ``D20160725-T205832.raw``
        finds the archive's ``HB1603_L1-D20160725-T205832.tar`` and the
        reverse. Applied after the time window, client side, in catalogue
        order. A name with no stamp, or one the query did not return,
        raises rather than silently shrinking the result. ``None`` or
        empty keeps everything.

Returns:
    dict: A dict with two keys:

        - ``records`` (``list[dict]``): One entry per file. Each dict
          contains all WCSD attribute fields plus a ``FILE_DATETIME``
          (``datetime`` or ``None``) parsed from the filename. Unless
          ``return_geometry=False``, each dict also carries a ``GEOMETRY``

inputs.description: Paths to .raw files to open. Entries may be local paths or remote fsspec URLs (e.g. gs://bucket/survey/file.raw). Each remote file is downloaded to a local scratch directory, converted, and the local copy deleted before the next file is fetched, so the machine only ever holds ~1 raw file at a time. params.name: sonar_model
params.description: Sonar model string recognized by echopype (e.g. 'EK60', 'EK80')

params.name: include_bot
params.description: Include bottom-detection (.bot) data if available

params.name: intermediate_format
params.description:
Intermediate store format written to exe_temp/data between the read_raw and combine_raw steps. Supported values: "netcdf" (default), "zarr", "none".
"netcdf" (default, recommended): each raw file is written as a temporary .nc file, reopened, and combined. After combining, all EchoData groups are rechunked to a single uniform chunk so the downstream zarr v2 checkpoint write (combine_raw with checkpoint: always) always succeeds.

source.doc:
Open raw sonar files and write each as an intermediate store.

Args:
    raw_file_paths: List of string paths or Path objects pointing to raw files.
        Entries may also be remote fsspec URLs (``gs://bucket/.../f.raw``).
        Each remote file is downloaded to a private local scratch directory,
        converted, and its local copy deleted before the next file is
        fetched — local disk therefore holds at most one raw file at a time
        (per concurrent instance), and bucket objects are never modified.
    sonar_model: Sonar model string for echopype (default: "EK60").
    include_bot: Whether to include .bot files (default: True).
    intermediate_format: ``"netcdf"`` (default), ``"zarr"``, or ``"none"``.
        ``"none"`` returns in-memory EchoData objects without writing any
        files.

        Pick by where the intermediates must live:

        ``"netcdf"`` is the default and the simplest choice for a *local*
        temp dir: each raw file is written to a temporary ``.nc`` file, then
        reopened and combined by ``combine_raw_stores``.  After combining,
        all groups are rechunked to a single uniform chunk so the downstream
        zarr v2 checkpoint write (``combine_raw`` step with
        ``checkpoint: always``) always succeeds.  HDF5 needs seekable
        writes, so netcdf **cannot** target object storage — a remote temp
        dir raises.

        ``"none"`` keeps every ``EchoData`` object in memory without
        touching disk.  Suitable when the full dataset fits comfortably in
        RAM.

        ``"zarr"`` is the option for surveys too large to stage locally: it
        is the only format that can write intermediates to a bucket, so a
        ``gs://`` temp dir requires it.  Stores are written with
        ``zarr_format=2`` and ``compress=False`` to match the checkpoint
        writer exactly; that is what avoids the v3-serializer and
        v3-BloscCodec errors a default ``to_zarr`` would trigger on the
        downstream v2 checkpoint write (see ``_open_and_store``).  Remote
        stores are staged to local scratch and bulk-uploaded, so local disk
        still holds only one store at a time (per concurrent instance).
    use_swap: Passed to ``ep.open_raw`` as ``use_swap`` (default: ``"auto"``).

Returns:
    list: Store path strings (zarr/netcdf) for file-backed formats, or a
    list of in-memory EchoData objects for ``intermediate_format="none"``.

ops.description:
Read a seafloor line from an Echoview ``.evl`` line file and align it to the Sv dataset's pings, returning a 1-D (ping_time,) DataArray in metres. Use it when a hand-verified Echoview bottom line is more trustworthy than running detection over the Sv data.
Echoview exports a survey as a series of part-day line files, so ``evl_path`` may be a folder: the files whose names span ``file_time_start`` to ``file_time_end`` are selected and concatenated into one line before interpolation. Give it the same window that selected the raw files.
Drop-in swap with the ``detect_seafloor`` and ``ep_detect_seafloor`` ops: the output port name (``seafloor_depth``) and shape (1-D, ping_time) match, so downstream steps such as ``create_seafloor_mask`` work unchanged. The recipe step's ``inputs`` drop the ``echodata`` line (no detection is run) and the ``params`` block takes ``evl_path`` plus the alignment settings below instead of ``channel`` / ``min_valid_depth_m`` or ``method`` / ``method_params``.
Pings the line does not cover come back as NaN, and ``create_seafloor_mask`` rejects **every sample** of a ping whose seafloor is NaN (the metres-vs-metres comparison is False against NaN). The step therefore prints its ping coverage on every run; set ``min_coverage`` to turn a shortfall into a hard error, or widen ``edge_extend_s`` / ``max_gap_s`` if the gaps are benign.

inputs.name: ds_Sv
inputs.description: Calibrated Sv dataset supplying the target ``ping_time`` coordinate. Also supplies the vertical reference: pass a dataset that has been through ``ep_add_depth`` so the line can be matched to ``depth`` (metres below the surface), which is what an Echoview seabed line normally records.

outputs.name: seafloor_depth
outputs.description: Seafloor depth in metres, shape (ping_time,), on ds_Sv's exact ping_time coordinate. Always 1-D (no channel dimension), matching the output of the ``detect_seafloor`` and ``ep_detect_seafloor`` ops so downstream masking steps are interchangeable. NaN wherever the line does not cover a ping.

params.name: evl_path
params.description:
A single Echoview ``.evl`` line file, or a folder of them to select from with file_time_start / file_time_end. May be a local path or a remote fsspec URL (e.g. gs://bucket/survey/seabed_lines); remote files are read in place (no download) since line files are small. The must_exist check is skipped at validation time for remote URLs and enforced by the step at run time instead.
Mutually exclusive with ``window``: exactly one of the two is required.

params.name: window
params.description:
Mapping carrying the line path under ``window_key``, used instead of ``evl_path``.
This is the form a mapped fan-out needs. ${_item} is an all-or-nothing token with no attribute access - there is no ${_item.seabed_evl} - so a step mapped over a list of window dicts cannot pull the path out of the item as its own param and has to take the dict. Wire it as ``window: ${_item}``.
A window also supplies file_time_start / file_time_end when those are not given directly, so a folder of part-day seabed exports narrows to the window without repeating its bounds. Extra keys are ignored, and an optional ``label`` names the instance in errors.
Note that a window's path is NOT content-fingerprinted the way evl_path is: it arrives as a runtime value rather than a declared param, so re-exporting that line does not by itself invalidate the step. The upstream step that produced the window is what carries its identity.

params.name: window_key
params.description: Key the line path is read from when ``window`` is given. Defaults to "seabed_evl", which is what plan_dive_datasets emits.

params.name: vertical_reference
params.description: What the EVL depths are measured from. "surface" (the default, and Echoview's usual seabed-line reference) means metres below the water surface; "transducer" means metres along the beam from the transducer face. The line is converted to whichever reference ds_Sv carries - depth when ep_add_depth ran upstream, otherwise echo_range.

params.name: min_status
params.description: Drop line points whose Echoview status is below this value (0 = none, 1 = unverified, 2 = bad, 3 = good). When null (the default) every point is kept. Dropped points leave a gap in the line, subject to max_gap_s.

params.name: max_gap_s
params.description: Widest hole in the line, in seconds, to interpolate across; pings sitting inside a wider hole come back as NaN. A ping landing exactly on a line point always keeps that point's depth. When null (the default) holes of any width are interpolated across.

params.name: edge_extend_s
params.description: How many seconds past the line's first and last point to hold that point's depth. The default 0.0 does no extrapolation at all, so pings outside the line's time span are NaN - this is what keeps a line covering only part of a survey from silently asserting a constant seafloor over the rest. Set null to hold the end depths indefinitely.

params.name: depth_offset_m
params.description: Constant metres added to the line, for when the transducer draft configured in Echoview differs from the one baked into ds_Sv['depth']. Positive pushes the seafloor deeper.

params.name: min_coverage
params.description: Fraction of pings (0-1) that must end up with a finite seafloor depth; below it the step fails instead of silently masking the uncovered pings away. Default 0.0 never fails.

params.name: file_time_start
params.description:
Optional inclusive ISO datetime (e.g. "2024-10-12T00:15") selecting which line files in an evl_path folder to read, by the d{YYYYMMDD}_t{HHMMSS}-t{HHMMSS} span in their names. Pass the same window that selected the raw files so the line and the pings stay in step.
A file's span runs from its own name stamp to the *next* file's, not to the end stamp in its own name - Echoview's end stamp under-reports the line's real last point by about one raw file's duration, so trusting it would drop the export straddling the window start and leave the leading pings with no seafloor. Selection is name-based, so no line data is read (or downloaded) to filter. Ignored when evl_path names a single file.

params.name: file_time_end
params.description: Optional inclusive ISO datetime upper bound for line file selection. See file_time_start.

Read an Echoview ``.evl`` seafloor line onto the ping grid of ``ds_Sv``.

Drop-in replacement for :func:`detect_seafloor`: returns the same 1-D
``(ping_time,)`` line in metres, on the exact ``ping_time`` coordinate of
``ds_Sv``, so :func:`create_seafloor_mask` consumes it unchanged. Use it
when a hand-verified Echoview bottom line is more trustworthy than running
detection.

A thin wrapper over :func:`read_line_evl`, which documents every argument in
full. What this adds is the coverage warning: pings the line does not cover
are NaN, and :func:`create_seafloor_mask` rejects **every sample** of a ping
whose seafloor is NaN, so a short line silently empties the echogram.

Two ways to say which line. ``evl_path`` is the direct form. ``window``
takes a mapping and reads the path out of it, which is what a mapped
fan-out needs: ``${_item}`` is an all-or-nothing token with no attribute
access, so a step mapped over a list of window dicts cannot pull the path
out of the item as its own param and has to take the dict. A window also
supplies ``file_time_start`` / ``file_time_end`` when they are not given
directly, so a folder of part-day seabed exports narrows to the window
without repeating its bounds.

Args:
    ds_Sv (xr.Dataset): Sv dataset supplying the target ``ping_time``.
    evl_path (str | Path | list | None): A single ``.evl`` file, or a folder
        of them to select from with ``file_time_start`` / ``file_time_end``.
        Mutually exclusive with *window*; exactly one is required.
    vertical_reference (str): ``"surface"`` (default) or ``"transducer"``.
    min_status (int | None): Drop points below this Echoview status.
    max_gap_s (float | None): Widest hole to interpolate across, in seconds.
    edge_extend_s (float | None): Seconds past the ends of the line to hold
        the end depths.
    depth_offset_m (float): Constant metres added to the line.
    min_coverage (float): Fraction of pings that must have a finite depth.
    file_time_start (str | datetime | None): Window lower bound for
        selecting line files out of a folder. Taken from *window* when a
        window is given and this is unset.
    file_time_end (str | datetime | None): Window upper bound. Same.
    window (Mapping | None): Mapping carrying the line path under
        *window_key*, plus optional ``start`` / ``end`` bounds and a
        ``label``. Extra keys are ignored, so one dict can carry a whole
        instance's context.
    window_key (str): Key the line path is read from. Defaults to
        "seabed_evl".

Returns:
    xr.DataArray: Seafloor depth in metres, dims ``("ping_time",)``, named
    ``seafloor_depth``, on the ``ping_time`` of ``ds_Sv``.

Raises:
    TypeError: If *window* is given and is not a mapping.
    ValueError: If both or neither of *evl_path* and *window* are given, or
        if *window* carries no line path under *window_key*.

Write the finished calibration outputs to a directory the survey keeps.
Writes channel_mapping.yaml and calibration_provenance.yaml at the top of archive_dir, and one file per standardized channel under Standardized_Reports/ - the same files a local run writes to single_channel_calibration_files/. The channel files are named by each channel's calibration file key, which is what the mapping refers to, so the archive resolves against itself.
Everything is rendered from the data the standardization and mapping steps return, so a caller that never sees the run's outputs folder can archive what those steps handed it. Omit an input and it is read from the outputs folder of the run in progress instead, which is how a local run archives with nothing but a directory.
archive_dir may be a remote fsspec URL, which is the point for a client whose run directory disappears when the container does.

source.doc:
Write the finished calibration outputs to *archive_dir* for keeping.

Writes ``channel_mapping.yaml`` and ``calibration_provenance.yaml`` at the
top of the directory, and one file per channel under
``Standardized_Reports/``. The channel files are named by each channel's
``_calibration_file_key``, which is what the mapping refers to, so the
archive resolves against itself.

Any of the three content arguments may be omitted, in which case it is read
from the calibration outputs folder of the run in progress. Supply all
three and nothing is read from disk, which is how a caller with no access
to that folder archives what the earlier phases returned to it.

Args:
    archive_dir: Directory to write the archive into. May be a remote
        fsspec URL (e.g. gs://bucket/surveys/RL2307/calibration).
    single_channel_data: The standardized channels, as returned on the
        standardization step's single_channel_data output. Read from
        single_channel_calibration_files/ when omitted.
    mapping_dict: Each raw file's channels mapped to their calibration key,
        from the mapping step. Read from channel_mapping.yaml when omitted.
    provenance: The provenance report from the mapping step. Read from
        calibration_provenance.yaml when omitted.
    output_base: Calibration outputs folder to read anything omitted from.
        Defaults to the folder the run in progress is writing.
    calibration_outputs: Subdirectory name under the run's outputs folder,
        used only to build that default.
    overwrite: If True, replace an archive already in *archive_dir*.
    verbose: If True, print what was written.

Returns:
    dict with keys:
        - archive_dir: The directory that was written.
        - mapping_path: Full path of the archived mapping file.
        - provenance_path: Full path of the archived provenance report.
        - reports_dir: The Standardized_Reports folder.
        - channel_count: How many channel files were written.

Narrow a Dataset to a ping_time window, or to the union of several.

The user-facing entry point into a survey-wide Sv store.  A survey-level
recipe computes and checkpoints Sv once for the whole cruise; a user
recipe reuses that checkpoint and calls this to work on its own segment.

Cheap on a zarr-backed Dataset: ``sel`` narrows the dask graph to the
chunks the window touches, so only those are read.  Keep the window step
downstream of every step whose checkpoint you want to share -- step hashes
are a Merkle chain, so a window wired into an upstream step's params
changes that step's hash and every hash below it, and no two windows would
ever share a cached Sv.

Two ways to say the same thing.  ``start``/``end`` is the direct form.
``window`` takes a mapping carrying those two keys, which is what a mapped
fan-out needs: ``${_item}`` is an all-or-nothing token with no attribute
access, so a step mapped over a list of window dicts cannot pull ``start``
and ``end`` out of the item as separate params and has to take the dict
itself.  Extra keys in the mapping are ignored, so one dict can carry
everything an instance needs (a label, its line files, its raw file list)
while this reads only the bounds.

Args:
    ds_Sv: Dataset carrying a ``ping_time`` coordinate.
    start: Inclusive ISO datetime lower bound (e.g. "2024-10-15T13:38").
        None leaves the start open.
    end: Inclusive ISO datetime upper bound.  None leaves the end open.
    dim: Time coordinate to slice.  Defaults to ``ping_time``.  Binned
        products carry the bin's left edge under a different name, so a
        per-cell statistics dataset is windowed with
        ``dim="cell_ping_time"``.  The bounds are compared against whatever
        that coordinate holds, so it has to be datetime-valued.
    allow_empty: Return ``None`` instead of raising when the window
        selects no pings.  This is what lets the step be mapped over a
        whole survey's per-file Sv: most files lie outside any one window,
        and ``concat_datasets`` already drops ``None`` entries from a
        collected list, so the fan-in keeps exactly the files that overlap.
        Left False by default, because against a single merged store an
        empty window is a mistake worth failing on.
    window: Mapping supplying ``start`` and ``end`` instead of passing them
        directly, plus an optional ``label`` printed to identify the
        instance.  Mutually exclusive with *start* and *end*.
    windows: Several such mappings.  Keeps every ping inside at least one
        of them, in time order, each ping once even where windows overlap.
        This is the form a step mapped over per-file Sv needs to pull a
        whole set of dive windows out of each file in one pass: the
        instance sees one file and cannot loop over the list itself.
        Mutually exclusive with the three arguments above.  Empty windows
        are skipped silently; only the whole set selecting nothing is
        reported, through *allow_empty*.
    snap_to_bin: Bin width such as ``"10s"``.  Each window is widened
        outward to whole bins of that width before selecting: the start
        moves back to its bin's left edge and the end forward to the last
        instant of its bin.  Use it when the selection feeds a time
        binning step, so the first and last bins are averaged over all of
        their pings and a window ending just inside a bin cannot leave it
        empty.  Edges are aligned to the epoch, as ``compute_mvbs`` aligns
        them for any width that divides a day.

Returns:
    xr.Dataset: The ``ping_time`` slice of *ds_Sv*.  Returned lazily when
    the input is dask-backed.

Raises:
    TypeError: If *window* is given and is not a mapping.
    ValueError: If *window* is combined with *start* or *end*, if it
        carries neither bound, if the window selects no pings and
        *allow_empty* is False, or if
        *start* is after *end*.  Also if *windows* is combined with any of
        the single-window arguments, or is empty.

ops.description:
Convert manufacturer calibration files to standardized single-channel files.
Parses the EK60 .cal or EK80 .xml files in the calibration input folder, validates them against the standardized schema, and writes one .yaml per channel into single_channel_calibration_files/ under the calibration output directory. These per-channel files are what NCEI archives.
The parse is skipped when standardization.fingerprint.json shows the same manufacturer files already produced the files that are there. That sidecar answers to the manufacturer folder, so deleting a single-channel file does not bring it back, which is what the mapping step's "error" conflict workflow relies on.

inputs.name: frequencies
inputs.description: Unique channel frequencies in Hz, normally from record_raw_file_configs. Sets the channel order for EK60 (.cal) data and is optional for EK80. Recovered from the saved raw_file_configs.yaml when omitted.

outputs.name: single_channel_dir
outputs.description: Folder the single-channel files were written to. Wire it into build_calibration_mapping for the ordering dependency.

outputs.name: channel_count
outputs.description: Number of single-channel calibration files in that folder.

outputs.name: skipped
outputs.description: True when the existing files were reused because the manufacturer files had not changed.

outputs.name: single_channel_data
outputs.description: The standardized channels as data: {"channels": [...]}, one entry per single-channel file, each carrying the _calibration_file_key that the mapping is built on. Produced on the fresh parse, the reuse path and an override alike, so a caller can review the channels without reading the folder. Plain JSON types only, so it checkpoints as JSON rather than a pickle and stays eligible for the shared survey cache.

params.name: cal_input_folder
params.description: Folder of manufacturer calibration files (.cal for EK60, .xml for EK80). May be a remote fsspec URL, which is downloaded whole to local scratch for the duration of the parse.

params.name: output_base
params.description: Root directory the calibration artifacts are written under. Normally wired to initial_setup's calibration_output_dir.

params.name: cruise_id
params.description: Cruise identifier recorded in every generated single-channel file (e.g. "HB2407"), so a standardized file stays traceable to the survey it came from.

params.name: record_author
params.description: Name recorded as the author of every generated single-channel file. Part of the provenance the standardized format carries, not something the calculation uses.

params.name: short_filenames
params.description: Use compact names for the generated single-channel files. Set false for longer, more descriptive names. The names become the calibration keys the mapping is built from, so this participates in the reuse fingerprint.

params.name: overwrite
params.description: Re-parse and rewrite even when the sidecar says the existing files are current, forcing a clean rebuild of the single-channel folder.

params.name: verbose
params.description: Print the parsed parameters and the files written.

params.name: override_channels
params.description:
Write these channels as the single-channel files instead of parsing the manufacturer files. Same shape as the single_channel_data output: omit an entry to discard that channel, and edit values in place to correct them. This is how a reviewed and edited set of channels comes back from a caller that has no access to the folder.
_calibration_file_key is ignored on input, because filenames are re-derived from the supplied values and an edit can therefore rename a file. The channels are validated against the standardized schema before anything is written, and the folder is cleared first so a discarded channel leaves no orphan behind for the mapping to match. Folded into the standardization fingerprint, so changing them rewrites the folder, and a later run that parses the manufacturer files again clears what an override wrote rather than mapping both sets.
